claims.claim: Quintus Septimius Florens Tertullianus, known as Tertullian, was a Carthaginian Christian writer who lived approximately 155–220 AD.
He served as a presbyter (priest) in the church of Carthage and was trained as a Roman lawyer.
Tertullian composed the treatise On Prayer (De Oratione) around AD 192.
The work was written as a theological instruction on Christian prayer, following the disciplines of repentance and baptism and presenting a “new form of prayer” for New Testament believers.
It was addressed to the “disciple[s] of the New Testament” and to “blessed brethren,” i.e., the Christian community.
On Prayer survives in the Latin manuscript tradition and was transmitted in the Ante‑Nicene Fathers collection, with modern English translations such as the Rev. S. Thelwall edition.
